notes:
A clean Borghertz AF ladder with two real evidence points, [KI] Old gauntlets from the coffer and [KI] Shadow flames from the torch, so the mark walks Jeuno -> Sea Serpent Grotto -> Jeuno -> Castle Zvahl Baileys -> Jeuno on its own. The 'Item Reqs: Grotto Coffer Key -OR- Thief's Tools' is a genuine either/or and is modelled as items vs items_alt on the coffer step.

The coffer's name is the one loss. The page calls it only 'a Coffer' and never gives it a proper name, so that is what is recorded rather than the client's likely 'Treasure Coffer' -- inventing a name is the one thing this pass must not do. A human who confirms the live entity name can promote it and the step gains its marker. Its grid is null for the same reason: the page says 'one of the locations mentioned above' and lists none.

All of bullet 2's sub-bullets are routing (Unity Warp to map 4 (L-5), the Gold Door, the Mythril Door and its Mythril Beastcoin, or the Proto-Waypoint to map 3 (J-5)); the page itself calls both doors blank targets, which OBJECT_DENY drops anyway, so they stay in a note. Bullet 5 is explicitly conditional -- 'if this is your first AF' -- so Deadly Minnow and Yin Pocanakhu are optional steps in the page's own order. The 1,000 gil is left out of items: gil is not an inventory item the readiness check can usefully gate on.

The 'Two Additional Coffers' section is deliberately NOT steps. It says outright that those coffers are not required and that the quest is 'completed' once you have the hands -- they are two more armour pieces for a quest that is already over, and hanging them off the end of the ladder would put a marker in the Temple of Uggalepih for a finished quest.

  step 7: A ??? can never carry a marker; the rung is kept anyway.

notes:
A four-rung quest that begins with no giver at all: the header's Start is the bare zone 'Walk of Echoes', so start.npc is null and step 1 is the zone entry itself. That is the honest reading -- bullet 1 says zoning in is what fires the cutscene -- and it costs nothing, because the very next step is the Ornate Door, which is a real named object and carries the mark for the rest of the quest.

Selecting the door twice is two steps, not one. The first select grants [KI] Butterfly-shaped key and the second opens the battlefield; merging them would let holding the key claim a step you have not done. Both point at the same entity, so the player sees one marker either way and loses nothing.

The fight's zone is deliberately null. The page names the battlefield ('A Forbidden Reunion') but never says which zone it is, and Gloomscale and Gloomtalon exist nowhere else in the world, so a zone-less row that matches anywhere is safer than guessing Walk of Echoes and blocking the match. The page writes them as 'a Zilant (Gloomscale)' and 'an a Gallu (Gloomtalon)' -- Zilant and Gallu are the families, the parenthesised words are the names, and only the names are recorded.

Bullet 5 (Lilisette fights with you) and bullet 6 (the closing cutscene) are outcome and commentary, and bullets 7 to 10 under '== Gloomscale and Gloomtalon ==' are pure tactics -- Doom moves, Holy Waters, a Bio aura, Sudden Lunge. None is a step. There is no hand-in: the quest ends on the cutscene inside the battlefield, so the ladder honestly stops at the fight. The Trust-initiation requirement in Quest Reqs has no observable predicate and gates nothing here.

steps.note: in from the Grauberg (S) Veridical Conflux (F-5), or the Pashhow Marshlands (S) conflux (J-9) once Voidwatch has opened it. If you never left the zone after Champion of the Dawn you must exit by the conflux and come back. Trusts must already be unlocked or the cutscene does not fire.
selecting it again may hand you the cutscene for The Dawn Also Rises instead, which is a different quest and not a failure here
the same door, to enter the battlefield. If it refuses entry even though you hold the key, zone out and back in.

only players who have the quest active or have already won may enter; Trusts are allowed. Lilisette fights beside you and the battle is lost if she falls, though she may transform into Lady Lilith or Lilith Ascendant and heal herself. The zone is left null because the page never names the battlefield's zone. Winning gives the closing cutscene and the rewards -- there is no NPC to return to.

notes:
The walkthrough proper stops after 'travel to Monarch Linn' -- the rest of the quest is in the two sibling sections, and both of them really are steps. 'Fight Details' is the BCNM itself and 'Rewards' bullet 1 is the hand-in ('Return to Justinius after winning the fight'). Their bullets restart at [1], which each step's note says.

The permit is the one evidence point and it is consumed on entering the battlefield, so the ladder anchors on step 1 and then falls back on the session latch across the fight -- the same shape as Carbuncle Debacle's pendulums. It is not repeated as items on step 3: it is held by definition of having got it, and duplicating it there would gain nothing.

Mammet-800 count is null on purpose: one more spawns per two alliance members, up to nine, which is neither fixed nor observable.

ADVERSARY: the draft put items_partial on step 3, the fight. The fight has no item requirement of any kind, so there is no alternative there that could not be expressed; the flag has been cleared. The conditional it was meant for -- 2 Giant Scales through Riverne - Site #A01, 1 through #B01, none at all with the Riverne - Site #B01 home point -- belongs to step 2, the travel, and this pass may only remove, so step 2's flag is MISSING rather than set. Confidence is lowered to medium for that: the ladder is right, but a genuinely unmodellable gate is now recorded nowhere in the schema and a human should raise step 2's items_partial.

'Quest Reqs: Promathia Mission 4-2' is recorded in prev even though the page has no Previous field; it is a mission, not a quest, so cat/area/id are null. The Conquest-tally cooldown in Rewards bullet 2 is a cooldown, and the long Reward list -- Miratete's Memoirs, Armoire, mannequin parts and the page's own joke about worthless synth materials -- is not a step.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: This is the step the unexpressible alternative belongs to, but items_partial is false here in the draft and this pass may not raise it.

Through Riverne - Site #A01 or Riverne - Site #B01. Without the Riverne - Site #B01 home point that costs 2 Giant Scales through A01 or 1 through B01, an EX drop from Firedrakes and Ignidrakes; the home point cannot be seen from packets, so the scales are left out of items.

from the 'Fight Details' section, whose bullets restart at [1]. One Mammet-800 per two alliance members, maximum nine, so no count is recorded. They change stance when a PC enters the grassy arena and attack one minute later whatever you do; Yellow Liquid locks one into its current form. The fight ends when the last one falls. The permit is consumed on entry, which is why it is step 1's evidence and not this step's.
from the 'Rewards' section, whose bullets restart at [1]. Repeatable after every Conquest tally, which nothing in the packets reports.

notes:
A twelve-stop errand across both halves of Adoulin, and the whole point of authoring it is bullet 4: thirteen NPCs with no stated order between the Orders, so they share one group and all thirteen draw at once. A strict ladder would mark Jozhud and then nothing until you happened to walk back to him. The single internal ordering the page does state -- Jozhud 'followed by' Palomel for the Order of Haverton -- is kept in both their notes rather than split out, because the two are the same Order and standing next to each other.

Step 1 is a precondition, not part of the quest: the library card comes from Patient Snake in the Scouts' Coalition and is what lets you talk to Reja Ygridhi at all. ADVERSARY: the draft left it optional=false, arguing that the runtime treats accepting the quest as proof step 1 is done so the rung costs nothing. That argument is about the acceptance step, which here is step 2, not step 1, and AUTHORING.md is categorical that a precondition is never a ladder position. It is now optional=true. The rung is kept, so a player who cannot start the quest is still pointed at the NPC who fixes that, but it no longer claims a position in the ladder. The card is a KEY item (id 2411), not an inventory item -- the resolver rejects it as an item -- and the [KI] Twelve Orders dossier is the second evidence point, granted the moment you accept.

Two of the thirteen have latent-quest traps the page warns about and neither is observable: Palomel may be stuck behind A Thirst for the Ages (and may be skipped outright if you are on A Thirst for the Eons), and Ploh Trishbahk may be stuck behind Meeting of the Minds. Both are notes. Rigobertine may open a cutscene first and needs a second conversation. None of the thirteen gives anything you hold, so the group carries no evidence and the ladder relies on the session latch until the hand-in.

notes:
Read straight, this is a short ladder with one painful gap. The quest's only mid-quest observable is [KI] Star ring (tarnished) from the sarcophagus, and it cannot be used: res/key_items.lua has 'star ring' twice, ids 225 and 226, and the resolver refuses names that are not unique rather than guess. So step 7 records the cutscene honestly with evidence null and the ladder falls back on the session latch from the Holy Water trade to the hand-in. Recording it anyway with a made-up spelling would have been the wrong kind of confident.

The Holy Water is the only thing held that matters, and it is held TWICE -- Bki Tbujhja hands the flask straight back after the trade, so it is items on both step 2 and step 5 and evidence on neither. It never proves anything, because you have it before, during and after.

The sarcophagus is a generic name shared by the five unbroken ones in the room at (D-4), and that is exactly right here: which one spawns the NMs is random, so drawing all five is better than pointing at one. The three NMs are not named in the walkthrough at all -- Yum Kimil, Dog Guardian and Owl Guardian come from the 'Field Notes' section, whose bullets restart at [1]. The Malatigeat detour is the page's own '(Optional)' and is marked so. 'From this point on, the quest can be completed on any job' and the closing 'You do not need to be on Bard' are notes on the Bard gate, not steps; the runtime only tests the gate before the quest is started, which is when Bard is genuinely required.

CORRECTION (hard rule 7 rewritten): step 7 now carries [KI] Star ring as evidence, because bullet 5 of 6 hands the ring over mid-walkthrough rather than at completion, so its appearance in the header's Reward no longer disqualifies it; the name is written as the game's 'Star ring' -- the page's '[KI] Star ring (tarnished)' minus the wiki's state-qualifier -- since that is the only spelling the resolver answers, returning ids [225,226] with 'any id satisfies it', which means the record's opening paragraph and the flags ambiguous_key_item and evidence_unresolvable are now stale and a human may clear them, and the ladder no longer has to fall back on the session latch from the Holy Water trade all the way to the hand-in.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 7: That key item CANNOT be used as evidence: 'star ring' is two different key items (225 and 226) and the resolver rejects ambiguous names. It is listed in the header's Reward field, but hard rule 7 as rewritten asks whether the walkthrough hands it over before the last bullet, and bullet 5 of 6 does exactly that The name is recorded as the game's own 'Star ring', which is the form the page's '[KI] Star ring (tarnished)' carries with the wiki's parenthetical state-qualifier stripped: res/key_items.lua 225 and 226 are both en='star ring', and the resolver answers that spelling with ids [225,226] and the reason 'one key item per unit carried; any id satisfies it' it resolves, so the earlier claim that it refuses non-unique names is wrong for kind=ki. 'Star ring (tarnished)' resolves to nothing at all and would have cost the step its marker.

notes:
The best-shaped quest in this batch: bullet 2 says the three strands may be collected 'in any order', so they are one group of three, each in a different zone and each carrying its OWN key item as evidence. Holding a strand retires that member and the other two keep drawing -- which is the whole reason groups exist -- and no two members share an item, so hard rule 4 is safe.

Each strand is deliberately ONE step rather than two. Every one of them is 'examine the object for a cutscene, then come back and give it something', and both halves happen at the same entity, so splitting them would add a rung the player cannot be tracked through and would not move the marker one pixel.

What the strands cost: the Fey Blossoms trade only works between 18:00 and 6:00, and game time is invisible to the addon. The Writhing Flame wants ANY job Testimony -- twenty-odd different items, which no AND-list can express -- so its items stay empty with items_partial set; the page names only Scholar's Testimony, and only as an easy drop, so it is not written in as though it were the requirement. The page also says the strand cannot be got on GEO or RUN, which is a job EXCLUSION and jobs is an allow-list, so it is a note.

Start is kept as the header's Lehko Habhoka even though bullet 1 says zoning into Windurst Waters (S) is what fires the cutscene: he is a real NPC standing in the right zone, so the marker lands where the player must go either way. The [KI] Gleipnir the quest is nominally assembling is never held -- the page says so itself -- so it is not evidence anywhere. Velda-Galda takes three separate conversations and then one more after a game day; both rungs are on the same NPC, so the player sees one marker. The closing 'return to Crossroads of Time' is mission advice, not a step.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 4: it need not match your job, so no items list can express it and items_partial is set instead; the page names Scholar's Testimony only as a high drop from three of the four Orcs at (I-11) west of the East Ronfaure [S] Survival Guide.
